forum.title: STM32H723 GCC compiler Optimization problem
forum.best_answer_content:
This typically means that there is a flaw (or flaws) in your code - it’s relying on something which the C language does not guarantee.

Probably the commonest is omitting/forgetting `volatile` where it's needed.

Relying on timing of the C code is another.

The `-Og` level should give you good debuggability - see [here](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Optimize-Options.html#:~:text=Optimize%20while%20keeping%20in%20mind%20debugging%20experience.%20-Og%20should%20be%20the%20optimization%20level%20of%20choice%20for%20the%20standard%20edit-compile-debug%20cycle%2C%20offering%20a%20reasonable%20blend%20of%20optimization%2C%20fast%20compilation%20and%20debugging%20experience).

You could try that …

Your could also try `printf`-style debugging to see where your code execution differs from what you intended

<https://community.st.com/stm32-mcus-products-25/compiler-optimization-problems-112524?postid=485029#post485029>

CarloV
scraped_replies.author: carloV

scraped_replies.html:
No.

You’re just going to have to debug it to see what’s going wrong.

You could start with a code review to check volatile usage, timing dependencies, etc.

As well as the software debugger, use a scope or logic analyser to see what happens with/without the optimisation.
